pipeline: Reality Studio authored Sequence -> existing deterministic sequence evaluator -> Reality Build presentation candidate boundary -> target host

semanticOwners.realityStudio: Reality Studio SequencerSession and evaluateSequence() own authored timeline normalization, active/fired clip selection, authority/presentation separation and sequence frame roots.
semanticOwners.realityBuild: Reality Build currently owns spatial presentation candidate validation and VSR fixed-Tick lowering, but has no Sequence consumer or Sequence playback entry point.
semanticOwners.vsr: Visual State Runtime owns animation clip/layer/graph sampling and frame compilation after an explicit VSR animation option exists.
semanticOwners.rsr: Reality Simulation Runtime owns authoritative spatial state and Tick; it does not own authored presentation tracks.

realTargetEvidence.reason: The audit intentionally stopped before inventing a Sequence-to-VSR target mapping or a second browser evaluator.

missingCapability: RNCS has a deterministic authored Sequence owner and a deterministic VSR evaluator, but no canonical projection contract that carries an evaluated Sequence frame or explicit 3D VSR target binding through Reality Build into web/Android/native targets.
donorAdvantage: Studio already separates authority tracks from presentation tracks and seals sequence/frame roots; VSR already consumes fixed-time clip/layer/graph options. The missing seam can reuse both instead of adding a Build timeline evaluator.

candidateOptions.description: Studio remains the timeline owner; Build accepts a sealed evaluated Sequence frame plus explicit VSR target bindings and lowers only the supported animation presentation state through the existing fixed-Tick seam.
candidateOptions.tradeoff: Smallest ownership change and easiest evidence boundary, but authoring/export must produce an explicit frame projection and it does not by itself provide target-side timeline editing.

candidateOptions.description: Extract the pure Sequence evaluator into a shared runtime and embed it in Build targets so the target evaluates authored tracks against the authoritative Tick.
candidateOptions.tradeoff: Supports richer playback, but expands browser/Android/native runtime surface, replay/evidence contracts and the canonical decision about which track classes lower to each target.

currentWorkaround: Keep Studio Sequence authoring/evaluation separate and use the existing Build fixed-tick animation_policy candidate for explicit VSR clip/layer/graph selections; do not infer a Sequence consumer or map audio/camera tracks implicitly.
regressionCase: Studio tests prove authority_root remains distinct from presentation_root; the raw Build project has no persisted sequence, so claiming Sequence target execution would be an unsupported promotion.
boundaries: No Build, web, Android or native target Sequence execution is claimed.
The default sequence created inside a Studio session is not evidence that the raw project artifact contains a sequence.
The existing animation track payload shape is not a canonical 3D VSR binding; no clip/node/mask/weight mapping is inferred.
Audio cue-to-asset lowering remains separately blocked by RCL_GAP_RNCS_AUDIO_TARGET_LOWERING.
No K400 gate is promoted to PASS.
humanDecisionRequired: Choose whether the next candidate should lower Studio-owned evaluated frames through an explicit Build projection, or establish a shared target-side Sequence runtime and track capability matrix. This is a canonical authored-presentation/target-runtime owner decision, not a missing local implementation detail.
